tools.name: audit_page
tools.description: Full on-page SEO audit of a URL: title, meta description, canonical, indexability (meta robots, X-Robots-Tag header, and robots.txt), redirect chain, viewport, Open Graph/Twitter, heading outline and hierarchy, word count, image alt coverage, internal/external link counts, structured-data presence, plus a list of issues and a 0–100 score. Free, no API key. Set pagespeed=true to also attach PageSpeed Insights performance metrics. After presenting the results, ASK THE USER whether they want a professionally formatted PDF report; if they say yes, call export_audit_pdf with the same url (and same pagespeed/strategy).

pagespeed.description: Also run PageSpeed Insights and attach performance metrics (default false)

local.description: When pagespeed=true, force the local Lighthouse engine instead of Google PSI (no API key/quota; requires Chrome installed). Default false — PSI is used first and falls back to local automatically when it is over quota.

detail.description: When pagespeed=true, also attach the full GTmetrix-style detail layer under pagespeed.detail (all category scores, diagnostics, resource breakdown, suggestions, passed checks). Default false.

tools.name: export_audit_pdf
tools.description: Generate a professionally laid-out PDF report of an on-page SEO audit (score badge, summary cards, severity-colored issue list, metadata, content/structure, social tags, and optional PageSpeed metrics). Re-runs the audit for the URL and writes a .pdf to disk, returning the file path. Use this after audit_page when the user asks for a PDF report.

url.description: Page URL to audit and export (https:// optional)

path.description: Output file path (default: ./seo-audit-<host>-<date>.pdf in the current directory). ".pdf" is appended if missing.

pagespeed.description: Also run PageSpeed and include performance metrics in the report (default false). When true, BOTH Mobile and Desktop are included in the same PDF unless a single "strategy" is specified.

strategy.description: Limit the PageSpeed section to one strategy: "mobile" or "desktop". Omit to include BOTH in the same file (default).

detail.description: Include the full GTmetrix-style detail in the PDF (category scores, diagnostics, resource weight, prioritized suggestions, passed checks). Defaults to true when pagespeed=true.

tools.name: audit_site
tools.description: Site-wide on-page SEO audit: discovers the site's URLs from its sitemap (resolving a sitemap index into child sitemaps), runs the on-page audit on each page (keyless, concurrency-limited), and returns site-level aggregates — average/min/max score, pages with errors, site-wide gaps (missing titles/meta/H1/schema), a rollup of the most common issues, and a per-page table. By DEFAULT the response is compact: per-page rows carry score and issue counts only (sorted worst-first) to keep the payload small; set detail=true to get full per-page metadata and each page's specific issues. PageSpeed is NOT run per page (too slow across many URLs). Use audit_page or pagespeed for deep per-page performance, or export_site_pdf for a formatted report.

url.description: Any URL on the site (https:// optional)

max.description: Maximum number of pages to audit (default 50)

detail.description: Return the full per-page breakdown (metadata, headings, and each page's issue list) instead of the compact score/counts table. Default false — keep it off unless the full detail is needed, as it is far larger.

tools.name: export_site_pdf
tools.description: Run a site-wide audit and write a professionally formatted multi-page PDF report (overall average-score badge, summary cards, coverage, common-issues rollup, a per-page results table sorted worst-first, and a full per-page details section — metadata, structure, and each page's specific issues). Returns the file path.

url.description: Any URL on the site (https:// optional)

max.description: Maximum number of pages to audit (default 50)

path.description: Output file path (default: ./seo-site-audit-<host>-<date>.pdf). ".pdf" appended if missing.

details.description: Include the full per-page details section (one card per page with metadata, structure, and issues). Default true; set false for a summary-only report.

tools.name: check_robots
tools.description: Fetch and parse a site's /robots.txt — user-agent groups, allow/disallow rules, and declared sitemaps.

tools.name: check_sitemap
tools.description: Discover and summarize a sitemap (via /sitemap.xml or robots.txt): index vs urlset, URL count, and a sample of URLs.

tools.name: extract_schema
tools.description: Extract JSON-LD structured data from a page and list the schema.org @types found (plus any microdata itemtypes and JSON-LD parse errors).

tools.name: find_broken_links
tools.description: Check the links on a page with HEAD requests and report any that return 4xx/5xx or are unreachable.

tools.name: keyword_ideas
tools.description: Get related keyword/query ideas for a seed term via Google Suggest (free; related queries only, no search volume).

tools.name: pagespeed
tools.description: Run Lighthouse for performance score (0–100), lab Core Web Vitals (LCP, CLS, TBT, FCP, Speed Index, TTI), and top improvement opportunities. Default engine is Google PageSpeed Insights (hosted; adds real-user CrUX field data when available; keyless but rate-limited — set PAGESPEED_API_KEY to raise the quota), and it auto-falls-back to a LOCAL Lighthouse run if PSI is over quota. Set local=true to force the local engine (no key, no quota; needs Chrome on the host; no CrUX field data; runs headless Chrome silently).

local.description: Force the local Lighthouse engine instead of Google PSI (no API key/quota; requires Chrome installed; lab metrics only). Default false.

detail.description: Return the full GTmetrix-style detail: all four category scores (Performance, Accessibility, Best Practices, SEO), diagnostics (server response, DOM size, page weight, request count), resource breakdown, prioritized suggestions with descriptions, and passed best-practice checks. Default false.
